title: 论文框架图生成
description:
You are a professor-level researcher skilled in drawing scientific architecture diagrams for top computer vision conferences such as CVPR, ICCV, and NeurIPS.

Now that you fully understand my research on pose-guided image generation and multimodal pose expansion, you must design a high-quality scientific architecture diagram that illustrates the core logical workflow of the proposed framework.

The diagram should clearly present the complete pipeline of pose-guided image generation, including:

• input pose representation (2D skeleton or 3D pose)
• reference appearance image
• pose conditioning module
• pose-aware feature encoding
• generative model unit (diffusion / GAN / control network)
• candidate generation stage
• structural consistency evaluation
• multimodal filtering
• final generated image output

The architecture should visually demonstrate the closed-loop logic of the framework:

Input → Pose Analysis → Conditional Generation → Candidate Results → Structure Consistency Screening → Final Output

Each module should be drawn as an independent block with clear titles.

Possible visual units include:

• stacked rectangles
• trapezoid processing blocks
• encoder-decoder shapes
• dual-branch pipelines
• feature fusion modules

Arrows must clearly indicate the direction of information flow.

Each module should contain internal submodules such as:

pose encoder
appearance encoder
pose alignment unit
generation module
consistency scoring module

The diagram should look like a real architecture figure from a CVPR paper.

Design requirements:

• publication-ready scientific diagram
• vector style diagram
• balanced layout
• no large empty areas
• clearly separated modules
• readable labels
• color-coded module groups
• logical pipeline connections

Each module should have its own background color to improve readability and emphasize modular structure.

The layout must be suitable for academic papers and maintain a clean and professional scientific appearance.
